causes.text: A 7.2-magnitude earthquake struck Taiwan, disrupting transport and some factory operations across the island. Initial assessments suggested near-term supply chain risks across advanced manufacturing.

source_info.title: Taiwan earthquake sparks supply chain concerns; manufacturers assess impact

effects.text: TSMC said production largely recovered but investors priced near-term disruption and risk premia. Shares in Taipei ended lower as risk was repriced across suppliers and fabs.

source_info.title: Taiwan's strongest quake in 25 years leaves buildings leaning; TSMC shares end down 1.3%

causal_reasoning_chain.description: A powerful earthquake disrupted logistics and briefly affected industrial operations across Taiwan, including advanced manufacturing corridors.
Even with rapid recovery, investors repriced operational risk and potential shipment delays, applying a higher risk premium to exposed firms.
On 2024-04-03, TSMC shares in Taipei ended down 1.3% (down), reflecting the immediate-risk repricing after the quake.

rationale: The event increases perceived fragility of operations and shipment timing, affecting near-term sentiment.
counterfactual_analysis: Without the quake, investors would likely have maintained prior risk assessments, avoiding the same-session drawdown.

adversarial_confounders.text: Unrelated macro weakness in the broader Taipei market could have contributed to the decline.
adversarial_confounders.impact: This would make attribution less precise, but the timing aligns with the quake.

adversarial_confounders.text: Company-specific headlines at other suppliers might have spilled over to TSMC.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Cross-reads exist, but the island-wide event is the most proximate driver.

details.commentary: Concentrated advanced manufacturing capacity in Taiwan means that a major earthquake highlights the operational risk of relying heavily on a single dominant foundry supplier. The shock reminded customers and investors that supply interruptions can quickly disrupt production and margins, prompting a repricing of TSMC and its peers within an industry structure where alternatives are limited.
